title: Improve dedicated autoscaler priority burst controls and utilization reporting
author: Miguel Santos
release_notes:
- Added per-priority burst smoothing and reporting for the Dedicated autoscaler.
- New telemetry metrics for priority-level burst usage and queueing.
- Backwards compatible under a feature flag; no runtime config changes required for existing customers.
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets have transient burst demands that can exhaust token buckets for a given priority and cause downstream queueing spikes. Previous work added token-bucket smoothing and fleet-level utilization reporting; customers requested clearer per-priority guarantees and visibility (ENG-10234).

Summary: This PR implements per-priority burst smoothing in the Dedicated autoscaler and extends utilization reporting so the console and reporting pipelines expose priority-level burst consumption (tokens consumed, smoothing window, effective throughput guarantees). Changes are guarded by a feature flag (autoscaler.priority_burst_reporting) and are backward compatible.

Design: - Introduce a per-priority token-bucket layer that maintains independent smoothing windows for priority classes (P0/P1/P2). - Token refill logic is decoupled from a fleet-wide refill; each priority has an adjustable burst allowance and smoothing half-life. - Add new metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst.used_tokens, dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst.refill_rate, dedicated.autoscaler.priority_queue.latency_p95. - Emit aggregated daily/10m reports that feed the Console and billing pipeline for more accurate unit economics per priority.

Implementation notes: - services/autoscaler/priority_bucket.go: new implementation of the per-priority token bucket with deterministic smoothing using an exponential moving average. - services/autoscaler/manager.go: orchestrates priority buckets, enforces throughput guarantees and fallback policies. - pkg/metrics/metrics.go + exporters/prometheus: new metric names and labels; added tagging for customer_id, fleet_id, priority. - web/console/dashboards/dedicated_autoscaler.json: new dashboard panels for priority burst consumption and queueing breakdowns. - Feature flag: autoscaler.priority_burst_reporting (default off).

Testing & CI: - Unit tests for token-bucket edge cases and deterministic time progression added under tests/autoscaler/. - Integration test exercises end-to-end burst behavior under mixed-priority workloads using perf-canary harness. - CI initially failed due to a flaky TestAutoscalerSmoothing that assumed wall-clock timing; fixed by switching to a simulated clock.

Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature flag and deploy to staging. - Run perf canary on a representative Dedicated fleet. - Enable flag for opt-in enterprise customers, monitor metrics for two weeks, then enable for all Dedicated fleets with a staged rollout.

Notes: - No customer-facing API contract changes. - Ops will get a short runbook and a new Console section describing the metrics and how to interpret them.

Improve dedicated autoscaler priority burst controls and utilization reporting

Per-priority token buckets, smoothing logic, metrics, console dashboards, and tests.
Guarded by feature flag: autoscaler.priority_burst_reporting.
Related: ENG-10234
notes_for_ops: Runbook: docs/ops/autoscaler-priority-burst.md. Recommended canary fleet: dedicated-testing-us-east-1. Watch metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst.used_tokens and dedicated.autoscaler.priority_queue.latency_p95. Feature flag: autoscaler.priority_burst_reporting (off by default).
changelog_entry: Added per-priority burst smoothing and telemetry for Dedicated autoscaler (opt-in via feature flag). Improves stability under mixed-priority bursts and provides better utilization reporting for billing and SLOs.
